title: private-deploy-staging-lifecycle-and-artifact-provenance-notes
body:
Purpose:
This note captures a proposed staging-to-prod promotion lifecycle for private deployments (VPC/on-prem) with an emphasis on artifact provenance and verification. The goal is to make rollouts predictable for customers, auditable for compliance, and reversible with low blast radius.

Scope and assumptions:
- Applies to Redwood Private installs running ArgoCD/gitops-driven cluster manifests plus customer-managed Terraform bootstrap (VPC networking, EKS/AKS/PKS, or on-prem k8s).
- We assume container images are produced in CI in the hosted environment and pushed to a registry reachable by customer infra (or staged in airgap bundles).
- Customers may supply their KMS/HSM for signing or allow Redwood-managed attestations depending on contract.

High-level lifecycle (staging -> pre-prod -> prod):
1) Build and attest:
   - CI builds image, generates SBOM (syft), and runs unit+smoke tests.
   - CI generates an image signature (cosign) and an attestation (in-toto/DSSE) that ties git commit, image digest, SBOM id, and CI pipeline id.
   - Artifacts: image:<digest>, sbom:<sha256>, attestation:<uri>, provenance.json.

2) Push to registry + store metadata:
   - Push image to customer or Redwood-hosted registry (depending on contract).
   - Upload SBOM and signed attestation to an artifact store (s3 or artifact repository).
   - Record metadata in release manifest (release.yaml) that lives in the gitops repo. The release.yaml contains: imageDigest, sigRef, sbomRef, pipelineRunId.

3) Promotion to staging (auto):
   - GitOps sync picks up release.yaml in the staging branch.
   - ArgoCD Application for staging has a pre-sync hook job that fetches attestation and verifies signature (cosign verify-blob / in-toto verify).
   - If verification fails, the sync is rejected and Slack/PagerDuty alert fires.

4) Observability gated canary in pre-prod:
   - After staging smoke checks, automated canary config (Argo Rollouts) is applied in pre-prod: 5% → 25% → 100% per metrics policy.
   - Metrics: p50/p95 latency, error rate, tail CPU/GPU usage, token throughput, and quality regression signals (unit LLM-similarity evaluations).
   - Each ramp requires provenance re-check (artifact immutability check by digest).

5) Production promotion (manual or automated depending on SLA):
   - Promotion is either: a) merge release.yaml to prod branch (human approval) OR b) automated if canary metrics pass for X minutes and signed off.
   - Prod ArgoCD pre-sync verifies signature and attestation, but also performs KMS-backed key-check (verify signer key is allowed for this customer).

Artifact provenance checklist (must be present before any promotion):
- imageDigest (sha256)
- cosign signature or equivalent (signature key id)
- sbomRef and sbom checksum (sha256)
- build pipeline id + git commit sha
- declared SBOM tool and version (syft vX.Y) and source of base images
- optional: binary SBOMs for non-container artifacts (air-gapped ops)

Terraform module notes (bootstrap modules for private deployments):
- Module: redwood-private-bootstrap
  - responsibilities: create bootstrap VPC resources, private ECR (or registry), initial ArgoCD namespace, KMS key binding resource (where supported), and RBAC roles for Argo operator.
  - inputs (string): cluster_name, customer_id, region, registry_endpoint, kms_key_arn, base_domain
  - outputs (string): argocd_url, registry_credentials_secret_name, kms_key_id, bootstrap_sa_arn
  - constraints: module should be idempotent across runs, avoid mutable resource names that change across runs. Keep state locking via remote backend enforced (s3 with dynamodb lock or equivalent).
  - migration notes: when rotating registry creds we generate a new k8s secret and leverage ArgoCD to pick up new secret via sealed-secrets or external secret operator – rotation must be orchestrated with a preflight traffic-quiesce step.

Helm/Chart/Upgrade semantics (recommended):
- Charts should be templated with image digest pinning (not tags) to guarantee immutability. values.yaml must support both image.tag and image.digest with digest taking precedence.
- Chart hooks: pre-install hook -> run image-attestation-check (call cosign/in-toto)
- Use Argo Rollouts for traffic shifting instead of simple helm upgrade for any customer-facing endpoints. Provides weighted traffic split and automatic analysis.

Image signing and verification patterns (practical):
- Signing by build: cosign sign --key ksm://... or cosign sign --kms <kms-uri> (if customer's KMS is available). Store public key in a trusted location referenced by ArgoCD.
- Verification: pre-sync job runs cosign verify --key <public-key> <image>@sha256:... and verifies attestation predicate (in-toto).
- For air-gapped installs: produce an OCI index + image bundle + sbom tarball + signed manifest. Operator on customer side runs a local verifier and loads images into local registry.

ArgoCD/GitOps flow specifics:
- Repo layout: repo-root/releases/<customer-id>/<env>/<release-id>/release.yaml
- Argo Application uses path: releases/<customer-id>/<env> and is scoped to that directory. Avoid global apps that read multiple customer areas.
- Pre-sync hooks: verify-attestation (blocking), run-preflight-tests (optional), backup-k8s-manifests (kubectl get --export)
- Post-sync hooks: run-smoke-tests, push-metrics-to-observability, create-release-note (comment back to PR).

Preflight checks (to fail fast):
- Registry reachability and digest resolvability (crane ls or podman/pull check).
- Node resource check (GPU/CPU) against manifest requests.
- KMS policy check: signer key is allowed for this tenant.
- RBAC check: Argo operator has permission to patch services for traffic shifting.

Validation & canary metrics (examples):
- Latency p50/p95 for inference endpoint (thresholds derived from SLA)
- Error rate (5xx or model-level nacks) < baseline+epsilon
- Model quality quick checks: run 100 prompts from the smoke prompt set and compute metric (ROUGE/BLEU/embedding-similarity) against baseline -> drift must be within threshold.

Rollback checklist (quick):
- If canary fails: automatic rollback to previous Argo Application revision (Argo Rollouts rollback) and quarantine image digest.
- If full-prod fails: trigger rollback play issuing two steps: 1) change release.yaml back to previous digest and push to prod branch, 2) ArgoCD sync with force=false to preserve reversibility.
- Post-rollback actions: notify security and SRE, gather attestation data, open incident ticket with reproducible steps.

Runbook snippets (useful commands):
- Verify attestation locally: cosign verify-blob --key <pubkey.pem> --signature attestation.sig provenance.json
- Check image digest resolvability: crane digest <registry>/<image>:<tag>
- Argo rollback CLI: kubectl argo rollouts undo rollout/<rollout-name> --to-revision=<n>

Air-gap and offline considerations:
- Provide a "bundle" export format: images.tar (OCI layout), sbom.tar, attestations.tar, release.yaml (with digest references) and a signed bundle manifest (cosign).
- Provide a local verifier tooling package (binary) that customers run once to validate bundle signatures and then import artifacts.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Decide standardized format for release.yaml provenance fields (we currently have multiple ad-hoc variants across teams).
- Define retention policy for attestations and SBOMs (90 days vs 1 year vs customer-configurable).
- Policy around signer key rotation when customer supplies their own KMS – how to re-sign historical artifacts or mark them as legacy?
- Add automated LLM-quality regression tests to canary gating; need tooling to run prompt suites deterministically and cheaply.

Notes on incremental adoption:
- Phase 1 (Q4): opt-in customers only, enforcement on pre-prod, manual prod promotion.
- Phase 2 (Q1 next year): autopromote with strict metric gates for low-risk customers and SaaS-internal installs.
- Phase 3: full enforcement including KMS-based signing for enterprise customers with compliance contracts.

Appendix: example minimal release.yaml
  ---
  release_id: r-20250210-18
  imageDigest: sha256:abcd1234...
  signatureRef: s3://artifacts/attestations/r-20250210-18.sig
  sbomRef: s3://artifacts/sboms/r-20250210-18.json
  builtFrom: https://github.com/redwood-inference/service-api/commit/7f3a9d
  pipelineRun: ci/12345

Contact: aisha.patel@redwood.com (ownership for initial rollout notes)

End of note.
